title: Support Info
body:
How we handle tickets. Read it before you take your first one.

You're the first thing a customer sees when something's gone wrong. Act like it.

options.label: Handling Tickets
options.title: Handling Tickets
options.content:
Claim it so nobody doubles up. Read the whole ticket before you reply.

Answer the actual question. Pasted boilerplate is obvious and makes people angrier.

Escalate anything involving refunds outside policy, staff conduct, or partnerships. Close with a one-line summary of what got resolved.

options.label: Refunds
options.title: Refunds
options.content:
You can approve a refund when work hasn't started.

Escalate when the work was already delivered, when they're disputing quality, or when it's above your limit.

Check the order log before you promise anything. Never commit to a refund you can't actually authorise.

options.label: Escalating
options.title: Escalating
options.content:
Straight to HR: staff reports, threats or harassment, doxxing, chargebacks, partnership or bulk enquiries.

Ping HR in the ticket. Don't DM them, and don't argue with the customer while you wait.

There's no penalty for escalating something that turned out to be small. There is one for sitting on something that wasn't.

options.label: Tone
options.title: Tone
options.content:
Warm, direct, short. Most people open a ticket because something is unclear or broken.

Own mistakes plainly and say what happens next. Don't guess at deadlines you don't control. Don't go silent, a holding message beats nothing.

Keep internal disagreements out of the ticket entirely.
